items.headline: Six taken to hospital, about 120 evacuated after Sengkang HDB fire
items.summary: A fire in a third-floor flat at Block 125 Rivervale Street at about 4.10pm on June 12 sent six people to hospital with smoke inhalation and forced the evacuation of around 120 residents; Sengkang GRC MP Louis Chua said temporary housing was being arranged.

items.headline: About 80 firefighters battle chemical-waste warehouse blaze in Tuas
items.summary: The SCDF deployed about 80 firefighters and 20 emergency vehicles to a warehouse fire at 3 Gul Crescent in Tuas, alerted at around 3am on June 12; the blaze involving waste and chemicals was contained by about 7.44am with no injuries.

items.headline: HDB June BTO launch offers about 6,900 flats, including first Bishan project in 40 years
items.summary: HDB's June 2026 BTO exercise offers about 6,900 flats across seven projects in five towns, headlined by roughly 1,210 units at a new Lakeview project in Bishan, the town's first BTO in over 40 years, near Marymount MRT.

items.headline: Singapore's IMDA and Microsoft sign pact on safe access to frontier AI models
items.summary: On June 12 IMDA and Microsoft signed an MOU to jointly develop a white paper on how governments and critical-infrastructure operators can responsibly access and test frontier AI models, inked by IMDA deputy CE Kiren Kumar and Microsoft's Natasha Crampton.

items.headline: First batch of nine women officers commissioned at IMA in Dehradun
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu reviewed the Passing Out Parade at the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun on June 13, where 515 cadets were commissioned, including the first batch of nine women to receive a permanent commission; 34 cadets from 16 foreign nations also graduated.

items.headline: India's retail inflation rises to 3.93% in May as food and fuel costs climb
items.summary: India's CPI inflation accelerated to 3.93% in May from 3.48% in April, a fifth straight monthly rise, with food inflation at 4.78%, data released June 12 showed; the rate stays within the RBI's 2-6% band.

items.headline: Supreme Court calls homemakers 'nation builders', sets ₹30,000 notional income
items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled on June 11 that a homemaker's unpaid work must be valued at a notional income of at least ₹30,000 a month for accident compensation, raising one family's award from ₹8.43 lakh to ₹62.78 lakh; bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N.K. Singh.

items.headline: Noida International Airport set to open to commercial flights on June 15
items.summary: IndiGo will operate the first commercial flights from the new Noida International Airport at Jewar from June 15, with the inaugural service arriving from Lucknow, bringing online the long-delayed airport meant to ease pressure on Delhi's airport.

items.headline: Update: Trump says US-Iran deal to be signed Sunday; Iran disputes timeline
items.summary: President Trump said on June 13 a deal to end the US-Iran war is scheduled to be signed Sunday June 14 and the Strait of Hormuz would reopen immediately, opening a 60-day talks window; Iran's foreign ministry and the Revolutionary Guard said the framework was not finalised.

items.headline: US strike kills Tren de Aragua gang leader 'Niño Guerrero', Trump says
items.summary: Trump said a US military strike on June 12 killed Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, the 43-year-old Tren de Aragua leader known as Niño Guerrero, at a compound in Venezuela's Bolívar state in an operation Washington said was coordinated with Caracas; he had a US bounty of up to $5 million.

items.headline: Brazil held to 1-1 draw by Morocco at the World Cup
items.summary: Vinícius Júnior struck in the 32nd minute to rescue a 1-1 draw for Brazil against Morocco at MetLife Stadium on June 13, after Ismael Saibari put Morocco ahead in the 21st minute in their Group C opener.

items.headline: Qatar earn first-ever World Cup point in 1-1 draw with Switzerland
items.summary: Boualem Khoukhi headed home in second-half stoppage time on June 13 to cancel out Breel Embolo's first-half penalty, earning Qatar a 1-1 draw with Switzerland and their first-ever point at a World Cup.

items.headline: Pope Leo XIV's plane grounded in Tenerife as Spain's king lends his jet
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV's charter back to Rome was grounded by a technical fault at Tenerife on June 12, prompting King Felipe VI to offer his Falcon jet, CNN reported; the pope departed more than three hours late at the end of a week-long visit to Spain.

items.headline: US orders Anthropic to curb foreign access to its top AI models
items.summary: TechCrunch and Bloomberg reported that the US Commerce Department on June 12 ordered Anthropic to block foreign nationals from its two newest frontier models, days after launch; unable to filter users in real time, the company disabled them worldwide while disputing the security claim.

items.headline: Nvidia pitches new Vera CPUs to Chinese clients as H200 sales stay frozen
items.summary: Nvidia told Chinese customers on June 12 that its new Vera data-centre CPUs could ship as early as August and that they can start placing orders, pivoting to general-purpose chips not covered by US export controls while H200 shipments to China remain stalled, The Information reported.

items.headline: Coinbase debuts AI agents that can trade crypto and pay for research
items.summary: Coinbase launched agent accounts on June 11 that run inside ChatGPT or Claude via its server, able to trade spot and derivatives and to autonomously pay for research and compute through the open x402 protocol, days after Robinhood unveiled its own trading agents.

items.headline: Robinhood reports record traffic after SpaceX market debut
items.summary: Robinhood said it saw record platform traffic on June 12 in the hours after SpaceX began trading, with some users hit by latency and intermittent outages as roughly 263 million SpaceX shares changed hands in the first hour.

items.headline: ECB raises rates for first time since 2023 to counter Iran-war inflation
items.summary: The European Central Bank raised its three key rates by 25 basis points on June 11, lifting the deposit rate to 2.25% effective June 17, its first hike since September 2023, to stop an Iran-war energy-price surge from feeding broader inflation, and revised up its inflation forecasts.

items.headline: Bank of Japan's Ueda hospitalised, will miss June 15-16 policy meeting
items.summary: BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, 74, was hospitalised for treatment of an infected liver cyst and will miss the June 15-16 policy meeting, the first time a serving governor has missed one since 1998, with Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino presiding; markets still expect a hike to 1%.

items.headline: Gold slips below US$4,200, heading for a second straight weekly loss
items.summary: Gold eased below US$4,200 an ounce on June 12 and was set for a second consecutive weekly decline, as optimism over an imminent US-Iran peace deal cooled inflation fears and lifted expectations of higher interest rates.

items.headline: Update: Oil caps about 6% weekly loss as US-Iran deal nears Hormuz reopening
items.summary: Crude posted roughly a 6% weekly loss after WTI fell about 3% to near $85 a barrel on June 12, as a Trump official put 80% odds on a US-Iran agreement within days that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the blockade, unwinding more of the war-risk premium.

items.headline: India beat Afghanistan by 7 wickets in rain-hit 1st ODI
items.summary: India won the rain-reduced 25-over first ODI in Dharamsala by seven wickets on June 13 to lead the series 1-0, with Shubman Gill 84 not out and KL Rahul 39 not out in reply to Afghanistan's 194, built on Rahmanullah Gurbaz's 51-ball 102; Gill was Player of the Match.

items.headline: Raducanu beats Jovic to reach her first grass-court final at Queen's
items.summary: Emma Raducanu beat sixth seed Iva Jovic 6-2, 6-2 on June 13 to reach the first WTA 500 final of her career at Queen's; she will face Donna Vekic, who beat Britain's Katie Boulter, in Sunday's final.

items.headline: Russell wins Canadian GP sprint and takes pole for Sunday's race
items.summary: George Russell won the Saturday sprint at the Canadian Grand Prix on June 13 after a wheel-to-wheel clash with Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, then took pole position for Sunday's Grand Prix with a last-gasp lap at the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve.

items.headline: Shelton saves two match points to set up all-American Stuttgart final
items.summary: Ben Shelton saved two match points to beat Jiri Lehecka 6-7(4), 7-6(14), 7-6(6) on June 13 and reach his first grass-court final at Stuttgart's BOSS Open, where he meets defending champion and fellow American Taylor Fritz, who beat Alexander Bublik 6-4, 6-4.

fun_fact.headline: The Eiffel Tower grows taller in summer
fun_fact.body: The Eiffel Tower is measurably taller in summer than in winter. As the sun heats its puddled-iron frame, the metal expands and the 330-metre tower can grow by some 12 to 15 centimetres, leaning very slightly away from the sun. When the iron cools in winter, the tower shrinks back.

puzzle.title: The Wine and the Water
puzzle.body: Two identical glasses hold 100 ml of wine and 100 ml of water. You move a 5 ml spoon of wine into the water and stir, then move a 5 ml spoon of the mixture back into the wine. Is there more wine in the water, or more water in the wine?
puzzle.approach: Don't track the mixing; compare the final volume in each glass.
puzzle.answer: They are exactly equal. Each glass ends with 100 ml, so the wine missing from the wine glass is replaced by an equal volume of water, and vice versa, regardless of stirring.
